extracted.intended_audience: newspaper editors, journalists, media researchers, and educators interested in reader engagement and newswriting styles
extracted.subtask_description: Assessing how different newspaper writing modes (traditional, narrative, radical clarity, point of view) affect reader behavior (reading), learning (knowledge), perceived quality, and issue involvement using a field-experimental design and surveys.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reading (dependent variable)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether readers actually read the story — measured as the dependent variable 'reading'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measured via post-publication telephone surveys of zone readers and by giving packets to vocational-school students; used as a primary behavioral outcome to compare writing modes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge (dependent variable)
rubrics_metrics.description: Knowledge gained from the story — measured as the dependent variable 'knowledge'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessed in surveys and analyzed (including path analysis) to determine how reading translates into knowledge for each writing mode; note that paths from 'reading' to 'knowledge' differed dramatically by mode.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perceived quality ('quality' variable)
rubrics_metrics.description: Readers' judgments of story quality — the report refers to a 'quality' variable on which traditional stories scored well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use reader ratings gathered by survey to compare perceived quality across modes; consider that perceived quality may not predict reading or knowledge equally across modes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue involvement / engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: The degree to which a story gets readers 'involved in issues' (civic/issue engagement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measured separately from reading and knowledge; the narrative form scored well overall but 'failed to get readers involved in issues' according to the study — track engagement-specific items in surveys.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall positive/negative effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Net positive or negative reception/effects of a writing mode (e.g., 'radical clarity did not produce many outstanding positive or negative results', 'point of view mode' registered the poorest performance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare aggregate outcome patterns (reading, knowledge, quality, engagement) to determine whether a mode yields clear beneficial or detrimental effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing mode taxonomy
rubrics_metrics.description: The four distinct newswriting modes evaluated: traditional, narrative, radical clarity, and point of view.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produce sample stories in each mode for direct comparison; ensure consistent story facts while varying style so differences can be attributed to mode rather than content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness for specific reader subgroups
rubrics_metrics.description: How modes perform among younger, less educated, and less loyal-to-newspaper readers (the aliterate target groups).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include oversamples or targeted samples (e.g., vocational-school students reading packets) to obtain larger representation of these subgroups and compare mode effects within them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justification of predominant style
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the predominance of traditional stories is empirically justified ('traditional stories did not seem to justify their predominance').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare traditional mode to alternatives on multiple outcomes (reading, knowledge, quality, engagement) before concluding it should remain dominant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental / research design standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Design elements required to validly test writing-mode effects: same story written in different modes, multiple reporters, treatments assigned to contiguous circulation zones across days, and follow-up surveys.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use multiple reporters to write each mode to reduce author-specific effects; rotate mode-zone assignments across days; measure outcomes via telephone surveys and controlled packet-reading to strengthen causal inferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Path analysis of causal mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyzing the causal paths from reading to downstream outcomes (notably knowledge), since these paths vary by writing mode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct path analysis or other mediation models to reveal how reading leads (or does not lead) to knowledge and engagement for each mode; include figures/tables to represent these paths.
